:::{#exm-question}
#### Is the number at least 32?
<!-- no-figure: the example lists two sets, with nothing to plot -->

Let $X$ be [uniform](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-uniform) on the integers $0, 1, \ldots, 63$,
so that $\srcalph = \{0, 1, \ldots, 63\}$.
The question "Is $X \ge 32$?" has two possible answers:

- "yes", the set $\{32, 33, \ldots, 63\}$;
- "no", the set $\{0, 1, \ldots, 31\}$.

These two sets are nonempty and disjoint, and their union is $\srcalph$,
so they form a [question](#def-question),
and a [polar question](#def-polar-question).
If $X = 35$, the [answer](#def-answer) is $a(35) = \{32, 33, \ldots, 63\}$, that is, "yes".

:::
